answer_1.quote: In the past years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a transformative technology with applications in a large variety of social domains including medicine, finance, education and academia.
answer_1.outputs: The models generate free-text responses to political statements, which are then analyzed for political bias along economic and cultural dimensions.

answer_2.quote: We use an additional model to detect the stance of responses... we collect a stratified random sample from the data to fine-tune the classifier... we compare the performance of the automatic stance classifier against these manual annotations.

answer_3.quote: We use GPT-4 to decide all labels used for bias computation... As a robustness check, two authors of the paper manually labeled a sample (N = 40) for verification... we reran our analysis with Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct.

answer_4.quote: Two authors of the paper independently annotate 264 randomly sampled instances of LLM answers for political stance. The two annotators have substantial agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.68) and disagreements are resolved in a discussion round.
answer_4.guideline: The labels assigned are: {agree, disagree, neutral, unrelated}.
